summary: Figma provides a structured OAuth 2.0 flow and API access for developers. Integration requires specific account tiers, local environment setup, and a formal review process for public apps. Developers must manage credentials securely and adhere to strict usage policies regarding user consent.

reason.text: Getting started requires specific account plan seats, Node.js installation, and manual configuration of OAuth credentials and project files.

claim.label: official_docs

claim.text: WebView access to the Figma OAuth flow is not supported.

blockers.issue: WebView access is not supported for the OAuth flow.
blockers.fix: Use a standard web browser for the authentication URL instead of an embedded WebView.

blockers.fix: Ensure the app requires explicit user awareness and consent for reading or modifying files.

claim.text: Apps that read or modify a Figma file without user awareness and consent may be rejected.
claim.label: official_docs

claim.text: Apps cannot require users to install separate packages that manipulate Figma on the Web or the Desktop App.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Figma Community Apps can only leverage official APIs provided by Figma and cannot require users to install separate packages that manipulate Figma on the Web or the Desktop App.

blockers.fix: Do not attempt to exploit the API.

claim.text: Attempts to exploit the API will result in immediate denial of API access.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Any attempts to exploit the API (deceitful manipulation of user files, theft of data) will result in immediate denial of API access.

blockers.fix: Do not use projects endpoints to enumerate files in an organization or team.

claim.text: Apps are not permitted to index file content available in a customer's account.

extras.why_it_matters: The provider offers more than one way to set up. Compare before you choose.

claims.text: OAuth apps allow acting on behalf of individual users, while plan access tokens are for organization-level automation.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Use an OAuth app if your application needs to act on behalf of individual Figma users, and for the Embed API. Use a plan access token for organization-level automation like CI/CD pipelines, logging, and other tasks that shouldn't be tied to a specific user.

claims.text: You must choose whether your OAuth app is private or public.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Decide whether you want your app to be private or public. Private apps are limited to your organization and don't require Figma approval. Public apps can be used by anyone with a Figma account and must be reviewed and approved by Figma.

claims.text: Figma recommends using template files for connecting design components to code.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: In this guide, we’ll get you set up with Code Connect CLI using template files — the recommended approach for connecting your design components to code.
